newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scania sees truck potential in E.Europe.
newsitem.headline: Scania sees truck potential in E.Europe.

text.p: Swedish truck maker Scania said on Friday that there was big potential for the truck market in the former communist countries in Europe.

"In the long term (these countries) are a really important part of future volume increases and we are hoping to establish ourselves there," Urban Erdtman, head of Scania's European sales, told Reuters at a truck show in Brussels.
He named Poland as one market that Scania is targeting. Last year total sales there rose to over 3,000 trucks of which Scania has a slice of about 14 percent.
The Czech Republic and Hungary were two other interesting markets, he said.
"There we see strong growth," Erdtman said.
Russia has not yet shown signs of rising. Erdtman said that sales there are still rather thin and Scania has a market shares of about 12-13 percent.
In the Ukraine sales are picking up.
"We have already sold about 100 cars," he said.
